title: Three Daily Servings of Full-Fat Dairy Did Not Worsen Weight or Cholesterol in 12-Week Trial
dek: A University of Toronto study in The Journal of Nutrition found adults with overweight or obesity who ate three full-fat dairy servings a day saw no harm to weight, cholesterol or insulin resistance, and some saw blood pressure gains.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Empty 1923 milk bottle from the Allentown Dairy in Allentown, Pennsylvania
image.credit: Self Scanned, unknown credit / Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: Adults who ate three servings of full-fat dairy a day for 12 weeks did not show harmful changes in body weight, body composition, energy metabolism or blood cholesterol, compared with a low-dairy diet.
Participants who consumed more dairy showed improvements in blood pressure and greater intake of several key nutrients.
The trial enrolled adults with overweight and obesity; the findings do not directly address people with other health profiles.
The study was published in The Journal of Nutrition and led by University of Toronto professor Harvey Anderson.
body:
A 12-week trial suggests that three daily servings of full-fat dairy do not worsen weight, cholesterol or insulin resistance, challenging long-standing advice to choose low-fat dairy.

## What the study tested

The research, led by University of Toronto professor Harvey Anderson and published in The Journal of Nutrition, studied adults with overweight and obesity. Participants who ate three servings of full-fat dairy each day were compared with participants on a diet containing little dairy. According to the study record, researchers measured body weight, body composition, energy metabolism, blood lipids and dietary intake.

The design matters for how the result should be read. This was a controlled comparison over a fixed period, not a long-term observational study of what people eat in daily life. That makes it a useful check on the short-term metabolic effects of full-fat dairy, but it cannot answer questions about decades of consumption.

## What they found

The full-fat group did not show harmful changes in body weight, body composition, energy metabolism or blood cholesterol, according to the University of Toronto summary carried by ScienceDaily. The team also reported improvements in blood pressure and higher intake of several important nutrients among participants who consumed more dairy.

## Why the advice has been low-fat

Guidance in Canada and many other countries has favored low-fat or fat-free dairy, mainly because of saturated fat's effect on LDL cholesterol. LDL can contribute to fatty deposits in the arteries over time, which raises the risk of heart attacks and strokes. The new trial did not find that full-fat dairy raised blood cholesterol over 12 weeks, which is why the authors say the question deserves another look.

## Why it is not the final word

A single 12-week trial in adults with overweight or obesity does not show long-term cardiovascular outcomes, and it does not settle the question for people with other conditions, including those with existing heart disease or who need to limit saturated fat for medical reasons. The authors frame the results as a reason to revisit recommendations, not as a green light for any particular diet.

## What to watch

Longer trials that track heart events, and replication in more varied populations, would be needed before dietary guidance changes. Readers who have been advised to limit dairy fat should talk with their own clinicians before changing their intake.
